title: Trump Sells Early Access to Official Statements for Up to $100,000
description_short: Trump Sells Early Access to Official Statements for Up to $100,000
description_medium: President Donald Trump's official statements on Truth Social are considered presidential records and public property. However, Trump Media & Technology Group, which owns Truth Social, has announced it is charging up to $100,000 for early access to these statements. This move has been criticized as a broader assault on presidential recordkeeping. Trump's statements on Truth Social include announcements of sweeping tariffs, escalating threats against Iran, and Cabinet changes.
description_long: Trump Media & Technology Group announced a paid, licensed Truth API feed intended to give banks and trading firms faster access to posts from the ten most influential Truth Social accounts. Reuters reported that, before the launch, the company had discussed charging up to $100,000 per month, or $60,000 monthly for a three-year commitment. Reuters also reported that the company said customers had signed up ahead of launch, but did not identify them; the reported offer prices came from unnamed sources. The product raises questions about whether financial firms can receive Trump’s posts before ordinary users and news outlets, particularly when posts announce tariffs or other government actions. A press-freedom group and a media outlet later sued, arguing that the feed sold government information; Trump Media responded that the posts were widely available. The sources establish a commercial data product and reported pricing, but they do not provide an official determination that each post is a presidential record or establish that the service violated records law. The legal status of the posts and the boundaries between the company’s feed and government records remain unresolved.

title: Trump Defends Ballroom to Supreme Court as Military Complex
description_short: Trump Defends Ballroom to Supreme Court as Military Complex
description_medium: Donald Trump asked the Supreme Court for emergency permission to continue constructing a proposed White House ballroom while the legal challenge proceeds. Two lower courts had found that construction was proceeding without congressional authorization, and an appeals ruling would block most above-ground work beginning August 21 unless the justices intervened. The project includes an underground security bunker.
description_long: Donald Trump asked the Supreme Court to let construction of a proposed White House ballroom continue while a legal challenge proceeded. Two lower courts had ruled that the project was moving forward without congressional authorization. Trump’s emergency request sought permission to keep building without restrictions; an appeals court order blocking most above-ground work was due to take effect August 21 unless the Supreme Court intervened. The planned addition was described as about 90,000 square feet, larger than the White House mansion and West Wing combined, with a security bunker beneath it. Trump had demolished the East Wing to make way for the structure. Related reporting described the underground facilities as a military complex, while Trump called opponents of the ballroom disloyal to the country. The dispute placed the construction project before the justices on an urgent schedule. The request was not itself a Supreme Court ruling, and the reports do not establish the eventual outcome of the emergency application.

title: FBI Letter Allegedly Links Trump to Epstein and Saudi Trafficking Ring
description_short: FBI Letter Allegedly Links Trump to Epstein and Saudi Trafficking Ring
description_medium: IBTimes UK reported that commentator Kyle Kulinski presented a purported handwritten statement said to be among Epstein-related material released by the Justice Department. The text alleged Donald Trump was involved in selling young women to Jeffrey Epstein and a Saudi trafficking network. It was a reported allegation, not a finding of fact.
description_long: IBTimes UK traced the allegation to a handwritten statement presented by political commentator Kyle Kulinski on his show on August 19. Kulinski said the document appeared in Justice Department material concerning Jeffrey Epstein. The statement’s reported wording accused Donald Trump of involvement in selling young women to Epstein and a Saudi trafficking network. The article stressed that an FBI intake document or witness statement records an allegation and does not establish that the events described occurred. It also recounted a separate handwritten note containing allegations about a pregnant young woman, which the program discussed alongside the first document. The supplied report does not authenticate the handwriting, establish who wrote the statement, or show that investigators corroborated its claims. The entry therefore concerns the circulation of a serious allegation in Epstein-related records and media discussion of its purported source. The document’s authenticity and the truth of its accusations remain unestablished in the material provided.

title: Judge Orders Monitors for Child Detention as Trump Administration Plans Expansion
description_short: Judge Orders Monitors for Child Detention as Trump Administration Plans Expansion
description_medium: The American Prospect reported that a federal judge appointed a special master and an independent monitor to track how long immigrant children remain in detention and report possible violations of the Flores settlement. The appointees must report quarterly but cannot issue orders or sanctions. The report also described market research for possible emergency facilities, with proposed capacity from 100 to 3,000 beds; officials said it was not a solicitation.
description_long: In August 2026, U.S. District Judge Dolly Gee appointed former U.S. Attorney Andrea Sheridan Ordin as special master and pediatrician Paul H. Wise as an independent monitor in litigation over immigrant children’s detention. The American Prospect reported that they would track detention lengths and report at least quarterly on possible failures to comply with the Flores settlement. They may alert ICE and Customs and Border Protection to violations and recommend that the court hold hearings or impose sanctions, but they cannot issue binding orders or sanctions themselves. The appointment followed declarations and allegations that children were held beyond legal limits and in poor conditions. Separately, the article described a government market-research meeting about possible emergency influx facilities, with suggested capacities ranging from 100 to 3,000 children. Officials said the meeting was not a solicitation. The report documents new court monitoring and preliminary planning for possible additional capacity; it does not establish that new facilities were approved, contracted for, or opened.

title: Says He Fired Comey Because of Russia
description_short: In a television interview, Trump said he decided to fire FBI Director James Comey because of the Russia investigation.
description_medium: In a May 2017 NBC interview, Donald Trump said he had been going to fire FBI Director James Comey regardless of the Justice Department’s recommendation. Trump discussed the Russia investigation and said he had asked Comey whether he was personally under investigation. His account contradicted the White House’s previous explanation that Comey was fired over his handling of the Hillary Clinton email inquiry.
description_long: In a May 11, 2017 interview with NBC’s Lester Holt, Donald Trump said he was going to fire FBI Director James Comey “regardless” of the Justice Department’s recommendation. Trump described Comey as a “showboat” and said the FBI was in turmoil. He also discussed the Russia investigation, saying he had asked Comey whether he personally was under investigation and that Comey had told him he was not. The remarks complicated the White House’s earlier explanation for Comey’s dismissal. Officials had said the firing followed concerns about Comey’s handling of the investigation into Hillary Clinton’s emails and was unrelated to the FBI’s inquiry into Russian interference and possible links to Trump’s campaign. Trump’s interview made the Russia probe part of his own public account of the decision, even as he said he would have fired Comey regardless of the recommendation. The interview documented Trump’s stated reasoning; it did not by itself resolve the legal or investigative questions surrounding the firing.

title: Vetoes Resolution to End Border Emergency
description_short: Trump vetoed a congressional resolution seeking to terminate his border wall national emergency declaration.
description_medium: On March 15, 2019, Donald Trump vetoed a congressional resolution that would have ended his national emergency declaration at the U.S.-Mexico border. Trump had invoked the emergency in connection with border-wall construction after Congress did not provide the full amount he sought. The veto kept the declaration in place unless Congress could override it.
description_long: On March 15, 2019, President Donald Trump vetoed a resolution passed by Congress to terminate the national emergency he had declared at the U.S.-Mexico border. Trump had invoked emergency authority in support of border-wall construction after Congress declined to provide the full amount he requested. The resolution was Congress’s direct attempt to end that declaration. By vetoing it, Trump prevented the measure from taking effect through ordinary passage; lawmakers could still override the veto, but only with the constitutionally required two-thirds vote in each chamber. The dispute brought the president’s use of emergency powers into conflict with Congress’s role in determining federal spending. The veto preserved the emergency declaration at that point, but it did not represent congressional approval of the underlying policy: Congress had passed a resolution to terminate it. The supplied record does not establish the result of a later override effort or provide details about individual funding transfers, so those outcomes should be treated separately from the veto itself.
